defineUNet

Source: R/segModels.R
defineUNet.Rd

Define a UNet architecture for geospatial semantic segmentation.

Usage

defineUNet(
  inChn = 3,
  nCls = 3,
  actFunc = "relu",
  encBlocks = "double",
  btnBlock = "double",
  decBlocks = "double",
  useAttn = FALSE,
  useSE = FALSE,
  useCBAM = FALSE,
  useRes = FALSE,
  useASPP = FALSE,
  useDS = FALSE,
  enChn = c(16, 32, 64, 128),
  dcChn = c(128, 64, 32, 16),
  btnChn = 256,
  dilRates = c(6, 12, 18),
  dilChn = c(256, 256, 256, 256),
  negative_slope = 0.01,
  seRatio = 8,
  cbamRatio = 8,
  cbamKernelSize = 7,
  expRatio = 4,
  stageLRs = NULL
)

Arguments

inChn

Number of channels, bands, or predictor variables in the input image or raster data. Default is 3.

nCls

Number of classes being differentiated. For a binary classification, this can be either 1 or 2. If 2, the problem is treated as a multiclass problem, and a multiclass loss metric should be used. Default is 3.

actFunc

Defines activation function to use throughout the network for the non-ConvNeXt blocks. "relu" = rectified linear unit (ReLU); "lrelu" = leaky ReLU; "swish" = swish; "gelu" = GELU. Default is "relu".

encBlocks

Block implementation for the four encoder blocks. Either a single value applied to all four blocks or a length-4 character vector, with entries "double", "dws", or "convnext". Default is "double".

btnBlock

Block implementation for the bottleneck: "double", "dws", "convnext", or "aspp". Default is "double".

decBlocks

Block implementation for the four decoder blocks. Either a single value applied to all four blocks or a length-4 character vector, with entries "double", "dws", or "convnext". Default is "double".

useAttn

TRUE or FALSE. Whether to add attention gates along the skip connections. Default is FALSE or no attention gates are added. Ignored (forced FALSE) when useCBAM = TRUE.

useSE

TRUE or FALSE. Whether or not to include squeeze and excitation modules in the encoder. Default is FALSE or no squeeze and excitation modules are used. Ignored (forced FALSE) when useCBAM = TRUE.

useCBAM

TRUE or FALSE. Whether to apply a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to each encoder skip connection before it is concatenated with the upsampled decoder features. When TRUE, useSE and useAttn are forced to FALSE. Default is FALSE.

useRes

TRUE or FALSE. Whether to include residual connections in the "double" and "dws" encoder, decoder, and bottleneck blocks and in the ASPP bottleneck. Has no effect on "convnext" blocks (always residual). Default is FALSE or no residual connections are included.

useASPP

Deprecated. Use btnBlock = "aspp" instead. If TRUE and btnBlock is left at its default, the bottleneck is set to "aspp". Default is FALSE.

useDS

TRUE or FALSE. Whether or not to use deep supervision. If TRUE, four predictions are made, one at each decoder block resolution, and the predictions are returned as a list object containing the 4 predictions. If FALSE, only the final prediction at the original resolution is returned. Default is FALSE or deep supervision is not implemented.

enChn

Vector of 4 integers defining the number of output feature maps for each of the four encoder blocks. Default is 16, 32, 64, and 128.

dcChn

Vector of 4 integers defining the number of output feature maps for each of the 4 decoder blocks. Default is 128, 64, 32, and 16.

btnChn

Number of output feature maps from the bottleneck block. Default is 256.

dilRates

Vector of 3 values specifying the dilation rates used in the ASPP module. Default is 6, 12, and 18.

dilChn

Vector of 4 values specifying the number of channels to produce at each dilation rate within the ASPP module. Default is 256 for each dilation rate.

negative_slope

If actFunc = "lrelu", specifies the negative slope term to use. Default is 0.01.

seRatio

Ratio to use in the squeeze and excitation modules. The default is 8.

cbamRatio

Channel reduction ratio used in the CBAM channel attention MLP. Default is 8.

cbamKernelSize

Kernel size for the CBAM spatial attention convolution. Must be odd. Default is 7.

expRatio

Inverted-bottleneck expansion ratio for "convnext" blocks. Default is 4.

stageLRs

Optional numeric vector of length 9 specifying a base learning rate for each stage of the network: encoder stages e1, e2, e3, e4 (each paired with its squeeze-and-excitation or CBAM module when enabled), the bottleneck, and decoder stages d1, d2, d3, d4 (in that order). When provided, call model$get_param_groups() to obtain a list of optimizer parameter groups with per-stage learning rates. Default is NULL (single learning rate).

Value

Unet model instance as torch nn_module

Details

Define a UNet architecture with 4 blocks in the encoder, a bottleneck block, and 4 blocks in the decoder. UNet can accept a variable number of input channels, and the user can define the number of feature maps produced in each encoder and decoder block and the bottleneck.

Each encoder block, each decoder block, and the bottleneck can independently use one of several block implementations via encBlocks, decBlocks, and btnBlock:

  • "double" — the standard double 3x3 convolution block (default everywhere). Becomes a residual double convolution block when useRes = TRUE.

  • "dws" — a double convolution block whose second 3x3 convolution is replaced with a depthwise separable convolution (dwsDoubleConv). Becomes a residual variant (dwsDoubleConvR) when useRes = TRUE.

  • "convnext" — a ConvNeXt-style block (depthwise 7x7, LayerNorm, 1x1 inverted-bottleneck expansion, GELU, 1x1 projection, residual; doubleConvBlkCNX). Always residual and always GELU, so useRes and actFunc do not affect these blocks.

  • "aspp" — (btnBlock only) a modified atrous spatial pyramid pooling module for multi-scale context.

Users can also choose to (1) replace all ReLU activation functions with leaky ReLU, swish, or GELU in the non-ConvNeXt blocks, (2) implement attention gates along the skip connections (useAttn), (3) implement squeeze-and-excitation modules within the encoder (useSE), (4) apply Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) to the skip connections (useCBAM), (5) add residual connections within the "double" blocks and ASPP bottleneck (useRes), and/or (6) implement deep supervision using predictions generated at each stage in the decoder (useDS). Because CBAM already performs both channel and spatial recalibration, setting useCBAM = TRUE forces useSE and useAttn to FALSE.
